subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `models auth login` fail closed with a gateway-host instruction, or should OpenClaw design credential forwarding/syncing to the gateway?
rationale: The current bug is clear, but syncing OAuth credentials over the node-gateway boundary would create a new sensitive credential-transfer path, while fail-closed behavior changes an existing CLI workflow.

options.title: Fail closed on node hosts
options.body: Block auth login when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the user to run the command on the gateway host; this is the narrowest security-preserving fix.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an explicit gateway API/protocol path for credential forwarding, accepting a larger security and compatibility design surface before fixing the issue.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep the current local-write path but add a warning, which preserves behavior but still risks consumed OAuth refresh tokens and unusable gateway credentials.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on node hosts
recommendation.body: Block auth login when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the user to run the command on the gateway host; this is the narrowest security-preserving fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the maintainer draft for this exact issue and has recent auth CLI history on the affected files.
